document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
text: Section 6 places duties on every employer that include keeping the workplace free from hazards likely to injure employees or cause occupational disease, complying with applicable occupational safety and health standards, and maintaining a reasonably practicable safe working environment without risk to employee health.

document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
text: Section 14 gives an employee a route to obtain workplace health and safety information and raise inadequate protection. Where an employee reasonably apprehends imminent serious injury, death, or imminent danger to health, the employee may notify the employer and the Inspector-cum-Facilitator; remedial action is required when imminent danger is accepted.

document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section: Sections 18 and 23 - Standards and workplace conditions
text: Section 23 makes the employer responsible for maintaining prescribed health, safety, and working conditions. The listed matters include ventilation and temperature, an environment free from dust and noxious gas or fumes, and measures against overcrowding. Section 18 concerns occupational safety and health standards.

document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
section: Section 84 - Compulsory disclosure for hazardous processes
text: For a factory involving a hazardous process, section 84 addresses disclosure of danger and health-hazard information and measures to overcome hazards to workers, authorities, and the nearby public. It also provides for an approved on-site emergency plan and detailed disaster-control measures to be made known to workers and the public.

document: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
text: Section 143 provides for repeal of listed enactments, including the Factories Act, 1948, from the commencement-notification date. The Central Government appointed 21 November 2025 as the commencement date for the Code. The Factories Act should therefore be retrieved as historical context, not represented as the current central statute.
